record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: For general β-ensembles, equivalently log gases at inverse temperature β>0, use the stochastic Schrödinger operator H_β = d^2/dx^2 - x - √(2/β) dB(x)/dx on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0 to obtain structural information about the edge statistics of the ensemble. In particular, derive the Tracy-Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue in the case β=2 directly from H_β.

evidence.quote: Part of the challenge in analyzing general β-ensembles is to use Hβ to obtain information about these ensembles.
Question: can one derive the Tracy-Widom formula for λ1(B; β = 2), say, directly from Hβ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let β > 0, and consider the stochastic Schrödinger operator (the stochastic Airy operator) defined formally by
  H_β = -d²/dx² + x + (2/√β) · B'(x),
acting on functions f ∈ L²((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition f(0) = 0, where B(x) is a standard Brownian motion on [0,∞) and B'(x) is its (distributional) white-noise derivative. (Equivalently, H_β = d²/dx² − x − √(2/β) dB/dx with appropriate sign conventions.) The operator H_β has a discrete spectrum, almost surely, with smallest eigenvalue λ_1(β); the random variable −λ_1(β) is the Tracy–Widom_β law and is known to describe the limiting fluctuation of the largest eigenvalue at the soft edge of the Gaussian β-ensemble (the log-gas at inverse temperature β).

Problem. Working directly from the operator H_β at β = 2, derive the Tracy–Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue, namely the identity
  P(−λ_1(2) ≤ s) = F_2(s) = det(I − K_Airy)_{L²(s,∞)} = exp(−∫_s^∞ (x−s) q(x)² dx),
where K_Airy is the Airy kernel and q is the Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II (q'' = x q + 2 q³, q(x) ~ Ai(x) as x → ∞), without invoking the determinantal/Airy-kernel structure of GUE as an external input. More generally, use H_β to extract structural information (such as a Painlevé/Fredholm-type representation) about the edge statistics of the β-ensemble.
artifact.category_tag: Stochastic Airy operator and Tracy-Widom distributions
artifact.status_search_result: The stochastic Airy operator was introduced by Edelman–Sutton and rigorously analyzed by Ramírez–Rider–Virág (2011), who proved that its bottom eigenvalues describe Tracy–Widom_β fluctuations for general β > 0. However, recovering the explicit Painlevé II / Fredholm determinant formula F_2 directly from the operator H_β (rather than from the determinantal structure of GUE) does not appear to have been carried out in the literature; the standard derivation of F_2 still proceeds via the Airy kernel determinantal point process. Subsequent works (e.g., Bloemendal–Virág on hard-edge and soft-edge PDEs, Rumanov on β = 6 Painlevé representations) give related characterizations but not a direct β = 2 Painlevé II derivation from H_β. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Beta ensembles, stochastic Airy spectrum, and a diffusion (Ramírez–Rider–Virág)
status_evidence.snippet: The Tracy–Widom_β law is characterized as the distribution of the lowest eigenvalue of the stochastic Airy operator.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the operator-theoretic characterization of TW_β, but does not derive the β=2 Painlevé II formula directly from H_β.

status_evidence.title: Tracy–Widom distribution — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: F_2 is given by the Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II via a Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel.
status_evidence.claim: Standard derivation of F_2 goes through the Airy-kernel determinantal structure, not through the stochastic Airy operator.

status_evidence.title: The Tracy–Widom distribution at large Dyson index
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on TW_β asymptotics still relies on the stochastic Airy operator characterization without producing a direct Painlevé derivation for β=2 from H_β.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to treat the operator-side derivation of explicit β=2 formulas as nontrivial.
